items.title: Bulk upload with a validation report
items.detail: src/upload.js holds the validator, the multipart parser and the collection contracts; GET and POST /api/v1/upload (src/routes/upload.js:53) serve the contract and accept multipart, text/csv and JSON through one validator with dry_run, a 20-error-capped row-level report and a refusal of partial import (src/routes/upload.js:53). Two spec items were deliberately not built and are documented as deviations in the ENH entry: it buffers under DEFAULT_MAX_BODY_BYTES instead of streaming to disk, and there is no client-side CSV picker (the only file input in public/ is a camera capture on the CHW surface, public/chw/index.html:545).

items.title: Two-way SMS acknowledgement, escalation, and delivery tracking
items.detail: No structured reply verbs anywhere: src/rapidpro.js parses inbound field reports and free text only, and no ACK/ESCALATE/RESOLVED verb or reason code exists in src/ or public/. There is no per-recipient delivery state, no delivery-report endpoint (the five rapidpro routes are status, response-metrics, dispatches, inbound, field-report — src/routes/rapidpro.js:72-76), and no escalation tree or acknowledgement SLA. The response_rate_pct rework at src/rapidpro.js:255 is the ALERT-05 fix, not this enhancement, and inbound webhooks are still written unconditionally with no idempotency guard (src/routes/rapidpro.js:194-200).
items.note: src/rapidpro.js. An anchored verb grammar (ACK/ESCALATE/RESOLVED/NAK) over a CLOSED set of reason codes; an unrecognised code is kept as reason_raw with reason_code null rather than invented. Correlation prefers an explicit id and otherwise matches the sender inside a bounded window — a reply that can close an SLA is attacker-controlled input, so it is never correlated by a payload-supplied alert_event_id, and the route sits behind the same webhook verification as a field report. reconcileInbound dedupes ALERT-06 against the same id shape the field-report route uses. Escalation fires only for dispatches the GATEWAY accepted, so our own outage cannot escalate; the clock runs from the first page for an alert; any reply counts as a response; a recipient already escalated is not escalated again, and the boundary is asserted exactly. Delivery stops at accepted_by_gateway because RapidPro v2 gives no per-recipient receipt — 'delivered' would be a claim the system cannot support. Uncorrelated replies are recorded and answered 202, because a wrong sender number is information. Served at /api/v1/rapidpro/reply, /delivery and /escalations. test/rapidpro-two-way.test.js.

items.title: Export that carries the narrative
items.detail: GET /api/v1/export.csv and /api/v1/export.geojson (src/routes/exports.js:83-84, 213) still return only the flattened source-record appendix — toCsv writes record keys and nothing else (src/utils.js:335) — with no warnings, no caveats and no pointer to export.md. No XLSX, no KMZ and no signed PDF exists in src/ or scripts/. markdown_download still records a byte count rather than the artefact (src/routes/reporting.js:546), and no per-row provenance stamp (source_id, observed_at, payload_hash) is added at export time.
items.note: src/reports.js renderExportMarkdown composes with renderReportMarkdown rather than reimplementing it, so the export and export.md cannot drift. Refusal vocabulary is imported from MODEL_BASIS rather than retyped. A withheld figure prints as 'not measured', never a dash in a column of numbers. check-no-flood-probability.mjs gained the rule the term list cannot catch — a null rendered, or a refusal named without its reason beside it — and fails the build on it. Served at GET /api/v1/kpi/quarterly.md; the PDF carries the same narrative page.

items.title: A donor-inspectable, hash-chained audit trail
items.detail: Two of the four parts shipped. The money path is now audited: the parametric writes write action logs with the token subject as actor (src/routes/parametric.js:132, 165, 183), asserted by test/parametric-trigger.test.js:300. action_logs is read-only by route guard — POST, PATCH and DELETE all answer 405 (src/routes/operational.js:87, 114, 139) — and a read-only audit view renders it in the workflow panel (public/workflow/panel.js:135, 168). Missing: there is no hash chain — prev_hash/row_hash appear nowhere in the tree, so tampering is undetectable — and there is no audit export a donor can inspect independently of the operator running the server.
items.note: src/audit-chain.js. verifyChain carries the RECOMPUTED hash forward as the next entry's expected predecessor and compares the stored field to that, so a consistently re-chained file is caught; the anchor is a head published out of band, and without one the result carries an `unanchored` advisory rather than passing. The preimage is a field whitelist including created_at, which canonicalHash drops. Covers the log, not the records (ADR-007). Served at GET /api/v1/audit/verify and /audit/head. test/audit-chain.test.js.

items.title: A store conformance suite, a real schema, and migrations
items.detail: Part 1 shipped and parts 2 and 3 now have: `src/migrations.js` is an ordered, idempotent migration runner with a frozen three-migration list, `SCHEMA_VERSION = 3`, and a `__schema` ledger. Each migration runs in its own transaction *and* records its own ledger row, so a batch that fails halfway leaves the completed migrations applied and recorded rather than half-applied and unrecorded — the usual alternative leaves the runner unable to tell which half it reached. `PostgresStore.ensureSchema` reads `schema_version` and applies `pendingMigrations(from)` instead of issuing hand-written `ALTER TABLE`s on every boot. Migration 3 adds the two generated columns the JSONB table was missing — `region` as `body->>'district'` and `observed_at` as a real `timestamptz` rather than a string inside JSON — with indexes on each, so the queries that were doing `body->>'…'` per row now use one. Still partial: the Postgres half of the conformance suite still only runs when `LINDELA_LITE_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is set and no CI job sets it, so CI measures one adapter against a contract written for two; the single `lite_records` JSONB table remains, with per-collection columns added only as generated expressions over the body rather than as typed columns; and the two stores can still diverge, since `JsonStore.remove()` and the Postgres equivalents are asserted separately rather than by one shared driver.
items.note: SCHEMA in src/store.js is one frozen declaration of {key, kind, derived, quarantines}; COLLECTIONS is derived from it and a test asserts that. assertDeclaredCollections runs at the top of write/merge/replaceAnalytics on BOTH adapters before any serialisation, so a refused write leaves the store usable. 40 record entries plus 6 quarantines generated from QUARANTINE_SOURCES. Migrations are versioned, ordered and idempotent with a recorded applied-version. Exercised against REAL Postgres 18.2 via test/pg-harness.mjs, which provisions a cluster and fails under CI rather than skipping — that found three shipped bugs, because every Postgres test used to skip.

items.title: API substrate: pagination, conditional requests, idempotency, readiness
items.detail: All five parts are in place and exercised by 31 passing tests. Cursor pagination with a total-count envelope is collectionPage (src/utils.js:210) at 27 call sites in src/server.js; ETag and 304 handling is in jsonResponse (src/utils.js:452-466); the Idempotency-Key wrapper is handleApi (src/server.js:923-1029), scoped by subject+method+path and replaying only sub-400 responses; GET /api/v1/ready probes the store with a timeout and reports mode, reachability and latency (src/server.js:1115-1210); and the OpenAPI document is diffed against the route table parsed out of src/server.js by scripts/check-openapi.mjs, run inside npm run validate (scripts/validate.mjs:264), which CI executes. One endpoint opts out of the envelope — GET /api/v1/kpi/snapshots returns a raw unpaginated list (src/routes/kpi.js:101).
